title: キュビスムの分類と作品の証拠
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: Editorial answers（編集・確認した解答）。元の本文・解説に基づき記述設問を英語4択へ変換しています。元記事の記述問題も引き続き利用できます。

passages.text:
A familiar summary says that Cubist artists showed an object from several viewpoints at once. The phrase is useful, but it can become a substitute for looking. In many works, a table, face, or instrument is divided into facets whose edges do not obey one continuous system of perspective. Some clues identify the subject, while other planes emphasize the flat support on which the image is made. The result does not simply reproduce what an eye sees from one position, yet neither does every plane correspond neatly to a photograph taken from another angle.

Art historians often distinguish Analytic and Synthetic Cubism. The first label is commonly associated with fragmented forms, shallow space, restricted color, and subjects that seem to dissolve into overlapping planes. The second is associated with larger shapes, stronger signs, and the incorporation or imitation of everyday materials such as printed paper and wood-grain patterns. These terms help comparison, but they were organized retrospectively and do not turn artistic change into two sealed boxes. Features overlap, dates vary by artist and object, and later works may reactivate earlier procedures.

Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque were central to the development of this visual language, particularly through an intense exchange of ideas before the First World War. Still, a history that treats them as isolated inventors hides other participants and conditions. Juan Gris developed distinct constructions; sculptors and painters transformed Cubist procedures; dealers, collectors, critics, exhibitions, newspapers, and commercially printed materials affected what could be made and seen. Influence was not a liquid poured in one direction from two sources. It moved through a network in which artists borrowed, resisted, translated, and displayed.

Collage makes this network of representation and material especially visible. A piece of imitation wood-grain paper may depict wood, remain a mass-produced scrap, and create a shape within a composition at the same time. The viewer must decide when a mark names an object, when it describes a surface, and when it points to the artwork's own construction. Cubism therefore changed more than the number of viewpoints. It made the relation among object, sign, material, and picture surface into an active problem. A strong interpretation begins with observable evidence in a particular work and only then connects that evidence to a broader movement.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Cubism can be fully explained by counting the viewpoints in each painting.

options.label: B
options.text: Cubism should be studied through observable works, flexible classifications, materials, and networks of production.

options.label: C
options.text: Analytic and Synthetic Cubism were two groups with no shared features.

options.label: D
options.text: Collage removed all references to recognizable objects.

questions.answer: The passage connects visual evidence, materials, flexible labels, and production networks. 正解：B。Aは視点の数だけに還元し、Cは分類の重なりを否定、Dは認識できる対象への言及を消しています。observable evidenceは「観察できる証拠」です。

questions.prompt: Why can the phrase 'several viewpoints at once' become a substitute for looking?

options.label: A
options.text: It prevents viewers from recognizing any object in a painting.

options.label: B
options.text: It proves that each plane is copied from a separate photograph.

options.label: C
options.text: It can replace observation of specific planes, subject clues, and the picture surface with a ready-made label.

options.label: D
options.text: It requires viewers to ignore the artists' names before examining a work.

questions.answer: A useful summary can become a label applied before observation. 正解：C。第1段落は各面と別角度の写真が必ず対応するわけではないと述べます。A・Bは根拠がなく、Dの作者名の無視も要求していません。substituteは「代用品」で、ここでは実際に見る行為を省くことです。

questions.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word 'retrospectively' is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: by organizing evidence after the developments occurred

options.label: B
options.text: by following a rule announced before any work was made

options.label: C
options.text: by copying a photograph from behind the subject

options.label: D
options.text: by removing dates and names from museum records

questions.answer: The labels were organized after the artistic developments they describe. 正解：A。retrospectivelyは「後から振り返って」。Bは時間の順序が逆、Cは視点との混同、Dの記録削除は本文にありません。後世の分類が無価値という意味ではありません。

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains both the value and the limitation of the Analytic/Synthetic distinction?

options.label: A
options.text: It establishes fixed dates that all artists followed, but says little about their materials.

options.label: B
options.text: It identifies two unrelated movements, but prevents comparison between individual works.

options.label: C
options.text: It proves that every later work abandons earlier methods, but cannot describe color.

options.label: D
options.text: It helps compare tendencies in form and materials, but treating the categories as sealed divisions ignores overlap and variation.

questions.answer: The labels help comparison, yet features overlap and dates vary. 正解：D。第2段落の比較の利点と境界の限界を両方示します。Aは日付を固定、Bは重なりを消し、Cは以前の方法の再利用に反します。sealed divisionsは「相互に重ならない閉じた区分」です。

questions.prompt: Which option combines the TWO kinds of evidence used to challenge the 'isolated inventors' account?

options.label: A
options.text: Picasso and Braque worked independently, and printed materials disappeared from painting.

options.label: B
options.text: Other artists transformed Cubist methods, and dealers, exhibitions, critics, and materials shaped production and reception.

options.label: C
options.text: Juan Gris rejected all Cubist methods, and collectors controlled every artistic decision.

options.label: D
options.text: All Cubist artists used identical forms, and newspapers determined the meaning of each work.

questions.answer: Other makers transformed methods; institutions and materials affected what could be made and seen. 正解：B。第3段落の二つの根拠をまとめています。Aは密接な交流に反し、C・Dは全否定や完全な支配を付け足します。receptionは「作品が見られ、受け取られること」です。

questions.prompt: Why is 'Picasso and Braque caused every later Cubist work' too strong a claim?

options.label: A
options.text: The passage denies that either artist influenced anyone else.

options.label: B
options.text: The passage says later artists only copied instructions from the two painters.

options.label: C
options.text: Influence moved through a network in which artists actively borrowed, resisted, and transformed ideas rather than receiving a single one-way cause.

options.label: D
options.text: Later Cubist works can be explained entirely by the chemical properties of paper.

questions.answer: The passage acknowledges their importance but rejects a one-way account of influence. 正解：C。借用・抵抗・翻訳・展示を行う受け手の能動性が根拠です。Aは影響自体の否定、Bは一方向への還元、Dは材料だけへの還元です。one-wayは「一方向の」です。

questions.prompt: What three roles can imitation wood-grain paper perform in a collage at the same time?

options.label: A
options.text: Representing wood, remaining a manufactured scrap, and forming a shape in the composition.

options.label: B
options.text: Providing three photographic viewpoints, replacing all objects, and removing the picture surface.

options.label: C
options.text: Recording the artist's biography, proving a fixed date, and identifying the dealer.

options.label: D
options.text: Becoming actual wood, eliminating signs, and hiding every material difference.

questions.answer: The same paper can depict wood, remain a real scrap, and contribute a shape. 正解：A。第4段落は表象・現実の材料・構図上の働きの三層を区別します。B・Cは本文外、Dは木の模様と本物の木を混同しています。compositionは「画面の構成・構図」です。

questions.prompt: Which statement best paraphrases the final sentence and explains why its order matters?

options.label: A
options.text: Start from a movement's name and infer unseen features, because labels are stronger evidence than observation.

options.label: B
options.text: Identify the artist first and disregard materials, because every member of a movement used the same methods.

options.label: C
options.text: Avoid comparisons with movements entirely, because particular works have no historical context.

options.label: D
options.text: Start with observable features of a particular work, then relate them to the movement, so that a label does not dictate what the viewer claims to see.

questions.answer: Evidence comes first; the broader classification follows. 正解：D。only thenは「その後に初めて」で、未観察の特徴を運動名から押し付けない順序です。Aは順序を逆転、Bは材料を捨て、Cは比較自体を禁じます。dictateは「判断を一方的に決める」です。

questions.prompt: Which plan best applies the passage's approach to evaluating whether an unfamiliar work is Cubist?

options.label: A
options.text: Count its viewpoints and accept the label whenever more than one can be imagined.

options.label: B
options.text: Examine object clues, spatial structure, planes, color, lettering, and actual versus depicted materials; then compare dated works and investigate the work's history.

options.label: C
options.text: Choose the closest famous painting and assume that similar geometry proves membership in the same historical movement.

options.label: D
options.text: Classify it from its date alone and disregard overlapping features or evidence about its materials.

questions.answer: Begin with the work, compare several features, and investigate historical evidence. 正解：B。元の発展問題の観察・比較・歴史検証を保持しています。Aは単純化、Cは形の類似を十分条件にし、Dは時代区分を硬直化します。depicted materialsは「描かれた材料」で、実物の貼り紙などとは区別します。
